review_notes: I read the whole file. It has four theorems, for rows 18 and 19 and for plus and minus. Each is closed by the single tactic `decide +kernel`, and none has a hand-written argument. The only repetition is that the same one-line tactic call is applied to different statements. The rubric calls that routine, so it does not count as repeated proof machinery. A shared lemma would need a single row-parametric statement, something like `∀ i k, base i.castSucc k + base i.succ k = fixedLiteralModPlus i k`. Proving that would need either a kernel decision over all rows, which is a different and heavier computation, or a new proof of the structure behind the tables. I did not look closely at the definitions of `fixedLiteralBaseMod` or `fixedLiteralModPlus`, so I can't say whether such a proof exists. The sibling files `FixedLiteralBaseRelationsRows*To*.lean` follow the same split by row pair. I only counted how often these names occur in them. I did not read their proofs. This looks like a deliberate split into small chunks, probably to keep each kernel computation small. Without evidence that a shared lemma would compile, or that the chunking is unintended, I report no justified finding.
